scope: Independent review of two candidate blueprints only

gates.C04: Exactly five fields per row changed: scenario, facts, boundary, level explanation and topic explanation. Tags, eligibility, runtime mappings, scope and structure match C04. No family proposed.
gates.topic: §4.2 supports reading the board, making movement policies explicit, and using service classes. The closed-record gate and safe hand-off are local facts. Explicit expedite priority can coexist with a physically non-preemptible action. The source defines lead time from request to delivery, including backlog.
gates.TC-135 decision: Closed record → ID → attachment → public opening. Doing B first lacks required ID. Opening first breaches the gate. A temporary override or equivalent representation of the same ordering is the same decision. Free staff and an empty queue disqualify a capacity intervention. Junior.
gates.TC-145 decision: Checkpoint at 4, finish at 9 ≤ 10. Interrupt now, finish at 17 > 10. Interrupting between now and the checkpoint also incurs 12 minutes before the five-minute return. Another worker is explicitly unavailable. Only the checkpoint strategy both respects expedited priority at first feasible handoff and meets the deadline. Junior.
gates.duplication: Reviewed historical nearest set and fresh production/planned retrieval for both IDs. TC-086/095/106/107 concern constrained review, blocked WIP and capacity, TC-013/091/234/298 concern distribution of demand or skills, TC-063 concerns admission to expedite. TC-222/287 choose extra work or a subset of the queue. Neither new decision repeats them. TC-039/110/150/158/199 change a structural dependency at another scale without a spurious reciprocal prerequisite. TC-093/213/214/240 vary risk and mitigation across exposures. TC-009/070/165 do not decide when to interrupt. Two proposed winners are also distinct.
gates.mapping: Swift mechanical derivation is correct for both input tag sets. Semantic scoring evidence still incomplete.

issues.finding: Primary structural-dependency-reduction is directly tested. bottleneck is a plausible negative diagnosis, but lead-time is neither observed nor used to choose. Generic benefit of removing waiting cannot support scoring prioritization.
issues.fix: Remove unsupported secondary tags and regenerate derived fields if governance allows. If tags are fixed, introduce an observed delivery-time decomposition and competing capacity diagnosis whose distinction materially determines the decision. Retest after removing those facts to see whether the decision changes.

issues.finding: With priority verified and recovery always mandatory, the earlier schedule dominates deterministically. The learner need only add durations. No independent risk distinction drives the selection, although runtime would score risk.
issues.fix: Either change classification under manifest governance or preserve risk-differentiation by making the known consequence of one interruption materially different by work state, with a credible trade-off and an explicit acceptance threshold. Test a counterfactual with unchanged effort, deadline and service class but changed exposure that flips the winner. Avoid reintroducing the TC-063 admission question.
